watches.description: SKU Code: W10/VHS The MWC W10S/VHS combines the distinctive appearance of the original hand-wound W10 with the accuracy and convenience of a modern VH31 sweep-seconds quartz movement. Its compact satin-finished stainless steel case, black dial and Admiralty Grey NATO strap preserve the character of the original military design. A Design Rooted in British Military Watchmaking The original hand-wound W10 preceded the quartz G10 watches introduced into British military service in 1980. At the time, plans to incorporate a quartz movement into the W10 case pattern were limited by the thickness of the movements available. A different case design was required, helping shape the G10 watches that followed. That lineage continues with the modern MWC G10 models supplied to the British Army through military procurement contractors . The final two images in this listing reproduce a government specification sheet dated February 1980 , inviting tenders for the W10 case pattern. Today’s slimmer quartz movements make it possible to revisit that original concept while retaining its distinctive proportions. Revived for a Military Procurement Requirement This model was developed following a request from a military procurement contractor for a substantial quantity of watches based on the original design. NATO codification was a requirement of the project. Following discussions with the MOD codification agency, it was agreed that the watch could use the original NATO Stock Number, 6645-99-541-5317 . Apart from the modern movement and the addition of a screw-down locking crown, the watch remains essentially faithful to the specification originally requested. The NSN is engraved on the caseback. HYBRID MOVEMENT – SMOOTH SWEEP WITH QUARTZ ACCURACY This watch is powered by a modern hybrid VH31 quartz movement. The movement is battery-powered and quartz-regulated but drives the hands in a smooth sweeping motion, offering a traditional mechanical appearance without the need for manual winding. In simple terms, it combines: The visual appeal of a mechanical watch The accuracy and convenience of quartz Accuracy is rated at ±15 seconds per month at normal temperatures —equivalent to approximately half a second per day when averaged over a month. This offers a significant improvement in timekeeping over the original hand-wound movement, without the need for daily winding. A hacking function stops the seconds hand when setting the time, allowing precise synchronisation. Practical, Understated Construction The case is manufactured from 316L stainless steel with a satin finish. A black dial with luminous markings provides clear readability, while the acrylic crystal retains the traditional appearance of the W10 design. A screw-down locking crown complements the watch’s 50-metre water resistance . Each watch is supplied with an 18mm Admiralty Grey heat-welded NATO webbing strap and a presentation tin. watches.description: SKU Code: AESCHBACH/AVI/2 This AESCHBACH Ltd Edition Classic Aviator Watch is one of their authentic WWII-pattern Pilot Watch models, designed to honor the timeless aesthetics of military timepieces from the 1940s and 1950s. The Classic Aviator Range is inspired by vintage military watch designs. While some models feature a subsidiary seconds hand at the 6 o’clock position—a hallmark of the 1940s—this model includes a sweep seconds hand , which became a popular replacement for subsidiary dials around 1943. This variety allows you to select a design that reflects your individual preferences. The watch’s imposing 46mm case diameter (excluding the crown) ensures a commanding wrist presence. The large dial size makes it extremely legible, both day and night, echoing the functional design of original WWII pilot watches. This model is powered by a reliable NH35A 24-jewel automatic mechanical movement , providing a 41-hour power reserve when fully wound. The clear caseback allows a fascinating view of the intricate movement inside. Specification Movement: Self-winding NH35A 21,600 BPH automatic, 24 jewels Case Diameter: 46mm (excluding crown) Thickness: 15mm Lug-to-Lug: 55mm Dial: Midnight Blue with luminous numerals and sweep seconds hand Case Material: 316L stainless steel Crown: Screw-down Water Resistance: 100m / 330ft Strap: 24mm high-quality stitched leather Crystal: Shatter-resistant and anti-reflective sapphire* Additional Details For historical reference, this watch takes inspiration from WWII German Luftwaffe watches . Why Sapphire Crystal? Sapphire crystal is a superior choice for watch durability and clarity: Strength & Scratch Resistance: Sapphire is incredibly durable, making it highly resistant to scratches and shattering. This is especially appealing for military personnel, security professionals, police officers, and outdoor enthusiasts—who comprise over 70% of our customer base. Accident Resistance: More than 90% of cracked watch crystals involve mineral glass. Even hardened mineral crystals don’t match the durability of sapphire under challenging conditions. Enhanced Manufacturing: Heat-treated sapphire glass undergoes stress removal for added strength. Each piece is coated with two layers of anti-reflective treatment to maximize visibility. Though sapphire crystal adds to the cost, its unparalleled durability and clarity make it a hallmark of premium watches. Its use in cutting-edge devices like the latest iPhone demonstrates its exceptional qualities. This AESCHBACH Classic Aviator Watch combines historical authenticity, modern engineering, and unmatched durability, making it a must-have for collectors and watch enthusiasts alike.

watches.name: Aeschbach Classic 1950s/60s Pattern Field Watch with a 24 Jewel Automatic Movement
watches.description: SKU Code: AESCHBACH MKIII This Aeschbach MKII field watch is a modern recreation of the classic 1950s NATO specification watches originally produced under the British Ministry of Defence reference 6B/346 Mk XI . While remaining faithful to the appearance and character of these historic military watches, it incorporates modern materials and engineering to deliver significantly improved reliability, durability, and performance. At the heart of the watch is a proven 24-jewel NH35A automatic movement featuring a 41-hour power reserve and hacking seconds function , allowing precise synchronisation of the watch. The movement is housed within a brushed stainless steel case inspired by the military watches of the 1950s and 1960s. Each case is manufactured and hand-finished in Zurich to ensure exceptional quality and attention to detail. Modern military organisations generally no longer procure watches to the standards that were once commonplace during the mid-20th century. Historically, armed forces around the world purchased watches from renowned manufacturers such as Rolex, IWC, Omega, and Longines. While such procurement practices are largely a thing of the past, there remains strong demand for military-pattern watches built to a higher specification. The MKIII was developed to satisfy that demand without compromise. The watch is fitted with a premium scratch and shatter-resistant sapphire crystal featuring an anti-reflective coating for outstanding legibility and durability. A screw-down crown and screw-down caseback provide enhanced protection against dust and moisture, contributing to the watch's impressive 100-metre (330-foot) water resistance . Combining classic military styling with modern engineering, the MKII offers an ideal balance of heritage, reliability, and everyday practicality. Specifications Case Diameter: 39 mm (excluding crown), 42.5 mm (including crown) Lug-to-Lug Length: 46.5 mm Case Thickness: 11.3 mm Weight: 73 g Water Resistance: 100 m / 330 ft Movement: NH35A 24-Jewel Automatic Movement Power Reserve: 41 Hours Hacking Function: Yes Luminous Material: Luminova Crystal: Scratch and Shatter-Resistant Sapphire Crystal with Anti-Reflective Coating Crown: Screw-Down Caseback: Screw-Down Strap Width: 20 mm Strap: NATO Webbing Strap Why Sapphire Crystal? One of the most common questions we receive concerns the advantages of sapphire crystal over conventional mineral glass. Synthetic sapphire is widely regarded as the finest material available for watch crystals due to its exceptional hardness and resistance to scratching and impact damage. These qualities make it particularly attractive to military personnel, security professionals, law enforcement officers, and outdoor enthusiasts, who represent a significant proportion of our customer base. In cases where watches are returned with damaged crystals, the overwhelming majority involve mineral glass, even when hardened mineral crystals are used. Sapphire crystals undergo specialised heat treatment to eliminate internal stresses, resulting in superior strength and durability. In addition, they are fitted with anti-reflective coatings that improve clarity and reduce glare in bright conditions. Although sapphire crystal is more expensive than mineral glass, its exceptional durability and long-term resistance to wear make it the preferred choice for premium-quality watches and professional-use timepieces. Historical Context: Aeschbach Watches Aeschbach, established in 1923, was one of many Swiss and German manufacturers producing military watches during WWII for the Wehrmacht, Kriegsmarine, and Luftwaffe. Collecting these historical timepieces can be challenging due to the sheer number of manufacturers involved, with over 100 suppliers identified to date. A group of military watch enthusiasts has compiled a nearly comprehensive list of these manufacturers, which can be accessed on their website under "WWII German Watches." watches.description: Product Code: SUB/MIL/SS/AUBL These diver's watches are a modern remake of a 1980s model that we produced until around 35 years ago. The watch features a robust stainless steel case and is equipped with a high-performance automatic 24-jewel self-winding movement. We have made several upgrades to the original design, including a shatter and scratch-resistant sapphire crystal and an increased water resistance rating. The dial and caseback are both unbranded (referred to as sterile in the military), giving the watch a clean and uncluttered appearance. Historical and Technical Background Inspired by the 1980 UK MOD specification for automatic diver's watches (DEF STAN 66-4 [Part 1] Issue 3), this model retains key design elements such as the unidirectional bezel and boldly marked dial with tritium paint. The original MOD specification also called for a mineral glass crystal, as documented in the MOD file shown in the final two images. While staying true to the spirit of the original, this updated version incorporates modern improvements, such as the use of non-radioactive paint and the inclusion of sapphire crystal, as detailed below. Key Features and Upgrades: Movement: High-performance automatic 24-jewel NH35A self-winding movement with a 41-hour reserve Crystal: Shatter and scratch-resistant sapphire crystal with anti-reflective coating Water Resistance: 300m / 1000ft Design: Sterile dial and caseback for a clean appearance Visibility: Uses Luminova for excellent nighttime visibility Strap: 20mm Stainless Steel Bracelet Specifications: Water Resistance: 300m / 1000ft Crown: Screwdown locking Caseback: Screw caseback Dimensions: Width: 45mm including the crown, 40mm excluding the crown Thickness: 15mm Crystal Diameter: 31mm Lug to Lug: 49mm Weight: 89.5g Movement: 24-jewel NH35A with a 41-hour reserve Strap: 20mm Stainless Steel Bracelet Packaging: Giftbox included Benefits of Sapphire Crystal: Many customers ask about the benefits of sapphire crystal over standard mineral crystal. Synthetic sapphire is extremely strong, shatter-resistant, and scratch-resistant, making it ideal for military and security personnel, police officers, and active outdoor enthusiasts. These groups account for over 70% of our customer base. Our observations show that over 90% of incidents involving cracked watch crystals occur with mineral glass. Even hardened mineral crystals do not match the durability of sapphire. Sapphire crystals are strengthened through a heat treatment process that removes internal stresses and are then coated with two layers of anti-reflective coating. Although sapphire crystals are more expensive, they offer superior longevity, resilience, and performance, justifying their use in higher-end watches. These models represent excellent value and are competitively priced for such a high-performance automatic watch. This watch combines the historical design and functional integrity of its predecessors with modern upgrades to meet the needs of today's professionals and enthusiasts.

watches.description: SKU Code: W10/265S MWC has been producing W10 models for decades, but this version is a recreation of the original 1960s–1970s pattern. Built for Endurance These automatic W10 models feature a heavy 316L military-grade stainless steel case . They’re robust, designed to withstand field conditions. The watch includes a sweep second hand , black dial , and luminous markings for excellent legibility. Unlike earlier models (and current CWC versions), this watch features a screw caseback for easier servicing — previous versions required crystal removal, which is considerably more difficult for many watchmakers. This led military watch manufacturers back to the drawing board — ultimately giving rise to the G10 range. The final two images in this listing show a government specification sheet from February 1980 , requesting tenders for this exact W10 pattern case. watches.name: MWC 1999-2001 Pattern Quartz Day/Date Military Divers Watch with PVD Stainless Steel Case and Sapphire Crystal on a Matching Bracelet
watches.description: SKU: DIV2001/DD/PVDBL MWC 300m Quartz Military Diver’s Watch with Black PVD Case and Bracelet Combining a classic military dial with modern materials, this MWC diver’s watch features a Swiss Ronda day/date movement, sapphire crystal and a matching black PVD stainless steel bracelet. Its uncluttered dial, luminous hands and markers, and 300m water resistance make it a practical choice for everyday wear and demanding outdoor use. MWC manufactured the original version from the early 1990s until 2004. Although the dial evolved during that period, the 1999–2001 pattern proved particularly popular for its clear layout and excellent readability in low light. This model retains that distinctive design, replacing the original tritium illumination with non-radioactive Luminova. Rediscovered and Reintroduced The decision to revive this watch followed an unexpected discovery by an MWC distributor in Australia. During a detailed stock check, the distributor’s son found 500 unused watches manufactured between 1999 and 2001 for a procurement contract. MWC was offered the opportunity to buy back the watches. Their popularity encouraged us to reintroduce the design, preserving its original character while upgrading key components. Modern Upgrades The current model incorporates several improvements over its predecessor: Sapphire crystal: Replaces the original hardened mineral glass, providing excellent scratch resistance and lasting clarity. 120-click bezel: Offers finer adjustment than the earlier 60- or 90-click versions. Swiss Ronda 517 movement: Provides day/date functionality and a nominal battery life of approximately 45 months. Black PVD Case and Bracelet The stainless steel case and matching bracelet feature a satin black PVD finish, giving the watch a subdued appearance with reduced reflections. PVD—Physical Vapour Deposition—creates a thin, strongly bonded coating on the metal surface. It offers excellent wear resistance and a durable alternative to conventional painted finishes. As with any surface coating, PVD can show wear through prolonged use or contact with abrasive materials such as rock or concrete. A Classic Military Diver’s Design The case closely follows the established pattern associated with Swiss case manufacturer MRP S.A. . With roots in the late 1970s, this distinctive design has a long history in military and professional diving watches. Related case patterns have appeared in watches from brands including Precista, Nilax, Elvia, Heuer and CWC. watches.description: Product Code: DIV82PV/AU/NDBL Overview This diver’s watch is a modern remake of one of our iconic 1980s military models, crafted with a robust black PVD stainless steel case and upgraded for today's demanding users. Originally redeveloped for a U.S. defense contractor, the watch features a 24-jewel automatic NH35A movement , a sapphire crystal , and a 300m water resistance rating . This version comes fitted with a matching black PVD stainless steel bracelet , giving it a bold, professional look ideal for both field use and everyday wear. Military-Grade PVD Finish The covert matte black non-reflective PVD coating is often specified in military contracts, particularly for special forces, anti-terrorist units, and covert operations . Unlike painted finishes, which can fade or peel, the PVD (Physical Vapor Deposition) process chemically bonds the finish to the steel at a molecular level , offering excellent durability under heavy use. While it can be damaged by deep gouges or extreme abrasion, it far outperforms lower-quality coatings in long-term wear. Historical & Technical Background This model draws direct inspiration from the 1980 UK Ministry of Defence specification for automatic diver’s watches (DEF STAN 66-4 [Part 1] Issue 3) . It retains key design features from the original, including the unidirectional rotating bezel and high-visibility dial , which was originally marked with tritium. In this modern version, tritium has been replaced with non-radioactive Luminova , and the mineral crystal has been upgraded to sapphire for greatly enhanced durability and scratch resistance. The final two images in the gallery include scans of the original MOD specification file. Key Features and Upgrades Movement: NH35A automatic, 24 jewels, 41-hour power reserve Crystal: Sapphire with anti-reflective coating Water Resistance: 300m / 1000ft Bracelet: Matching black PVD stainless steel Finish: Covert matte black non-reflective PVD coating Visibility: Luminova lume for excellent nighttime readability Design: Clean, sterile dial and caseback for a low-profile, tactical appearance Dimensions & Specifications Case Width: 45mm (including crown), 40mm (excluding crown) Thickness: 15mm Lug-to-Lug: 49mm Crystal Diameter: 31mm Weight: 89.5g Strap: 20mm Black PVD Stainless Steel Bracelet Caseback: Screw-down Crown: Screw-down locking crown Packaging: Supplied in a gift box Why Sapphire Crystal? Sapphire crystal is widely regarded as the best material for watch glass. It’s incredibly strong, scratch-resistant, and highly shatter-resistant , making it ideal for military, law enforcement, and outdoor environments. Over 70% of our customers come from these professional fields, and our experience shows that over 90% of cracked crystals involve mineral glass —even the hardened kind. Sapphire crystals are heat-treated to eliminate internal stresses , making them more durable. Each one is then finished with two layers of anti-reflective coating for enhanced clarity. The same material is used in modern iPhones, which speaks to its resilience and quality. While sapphire adds to production costs, it’s a hallmark of higher-end timepieces—and worth every penny in terms of long-term durability. Summary The DIV82PV/AU/NDBL combines rugged military heritage with modern-day performance , making it an excellent choice for professionals, collectors, or anyone seeking a tough, dependable automatic dive watch. Its striking all-black finish , military roots , and premium specs deliver exceptional value at a competitive price.

Designed around real operational requirements rather than cosmetic “dive styling,” this model combines 100ATM (1000m / 3,280ft) water resistance, a sapphire crystal, ceramic bezel and Luminova for first rate night time performance. Unlike many oversized dive watches, the Depthmaster is built to remain wearable for extended periods. Large military watches are frequently manufactured in titanium to reduce fatigue — the reduction in weight makes a substantial difference when worn daily for long durations, particularly on a 47mm watch designed for all types of diving from Scuba to Saturation diving. The watch uses a wider 24mm strap (most military divers use 20mm) for improved stability and security during active use, and the ceramic bezel offers excellent grip even in wet or extremely cold conditions. The PVD process creates a black finish on the titanium case that is vastly superior to painted finishes, which can easily fade or rub off. This PVD process means that the color of the metal is altered at a molecular level, ensuring it does not deteriorate even during heavy usage. However, the finish can be compromised if the case is severely damaged. Helium Escape Valve (Why It Exists) All MWC 100ATM models include an automatic helium escape valve . Helium molecules are extremely small. During saturation diving, they can slowly enter the watch case while divers live in pressurised environments using helium-oxygen breathing mixtures. When the diver returns to surface pressure, trapped helium expands and can force out the crystal or damage the crown. The one-way valve automatically releases the internal gas during decompression, preventing damage to the watch. This feature is primarily required by saturation divers . Most recreational divers will never need it, but a true professional-grade deep diver must include it to be fully fit for purpose. Sapphire Crystal The watch is fitted with an anti-reflective sapphire crystal. Sapphire is significantly more scratch- and impact-resistant than mineral glass and far more durable than acrylic. watches.description: SKU Code: ABACH/DUHR2S This automatic, self-winding military watch is a faithful reproduction of a classic World War II Aeschbach* design. It features a shatterproof and scratch-resistant sapphire crystal, a small subsidiary second-hand dial, and retains the timeless style used by the German Luftwaffe during the war. Originally issued to Luftwaffe pilots by the Reichsluftfahrtministerium (RLM/German Air Ministry) on a mission-by-mission basis, these watches were returned to the quartermaster after each mission. This modern version closely replicates Aeschbach's original WWII models. While the authentic watches are rare and command high prices, this updated version remains almost indistinguishable in appearance, featuring enhancements for everyday practicality. The acrylic crystal from the original has been upgraded to sapphire for improved durability, and the 15-jewel hand-winding movement has been replaced with a 21-jewel self-winding automatic movement that also allows for manual winding if desired. These subtle updates ensure greater reliability while maintaining the historic design. Designed around real operational requirements rather than cosmetic “dive styling,” this model combines 100ATM (1000m / 3,280ft) water resistance, a sapphire crystal, ceramic bezel and always on GTLS / tritium illumination. Unlike many oversized dive watches, the Depthmaster is built to remain wearable for extended periods. Large military watches are frequently manufactured in titanium to reduce fatigue — the reduction in weight makes a substantial difference when worn daily for long durations, particularly on a 47mm watch designed for all types of diving from Scuba to Saturation diving. The watch uses a wider 24mm strap (most military divers use 20mm) for improved stability and security during active use, and the ceramic bezel offers excellent grip even in wet or extremely cold conditions. This particular variant features a 24-hour military dial for quick time interpretation in operational or low-light conditions. Tritium GTLS Illumination The Depthmaster uses GTLS tritium tubes on the hands and markers. Unlike conventional lume, tritium does not require charging from sunlight or artificial light. The watch remains readable continuously, all night, every night and GTLS tritium tubes typically remain useful for about 20–25 years — making it especially suitable for military, security, aviation and maritime use. The bezel markings additionally use Luminova for high initial brightness when exposed to light. Helium Escape Valve (Why It Exists) All MWC 100ATM models include an automatic helium escape valve . Helium molecules are extremely small. During saturation diving, they can slowly enter the watch case while divers live in pressurised environments using helium-oxygen breathing mixtures. When the diver returns to surface pressure, trapped helium expands and can force out the crystal or damage the crown. The one-way valve automatically releases the internal gas during decompression, preventing damage to the watch. This feature is primarily required by saturation divers . Most recreational divers will never need it, but a true professional-grade deep diver must include it to be fully fit for purpose. Sapphire Crystal The watch is fitted with an anti-reflective sapphire crystal. Sapphire is significantly more scratch- and impact-resistant than mineral glass and far more durable than acrylic. In real-world service use, the overwhelming majority of cracked crystals occur on mineral or acrylic watches — sapphire dramatically reduces that risk. Movement The Depthmaster is powered by the reliable 24-jewel NH35A automatic movement with hacking function, allowing precise synchronisation. Power reserve: approximately 41 hours. Specifications • Movement: 24-Jewel Automatic NH35A with hacking (hand-winding capable) • Water Resistance: 100ATM / 1000m / 3,280ft • Crown: Screw-down, sealed • Helium Escape Valve: Automatic one-way release valve • Case Diameter: 44mm (47mm including crown) • Thickness: 18mm • Lug-to-Lug Length: 48mm • Case Material: Titanium • Crystal: Sapphire with anti-reflective coating • Crystal Diameter: 31mm • Bezel: Unidirectional dive bezel with ceramic insert • Illumination: Tritium GTLS tubes on hands & markers, Luminova on bezel • Lugs: Spring-bars • Strap: 24mm military NATO webbing strap (1 x Grey and 1 x Black) • Weight: Approx. 85g Designed for Real Conditions Professional divers, maritime personnel and military users often operate in cold, wet and high-pressure environments for extended periods. Watches in this category are intended to be reliable equipment rather than jewellery. The Depthmaster is built accordingly: high water resistance, continuous night visibility, shock resistance and simple operation while wearing gloves. This is not a fashion diver — it is a functional instrument watch engineered for harsh service conditions.

The original MOD specification also called for a mineral glass crystal, as documented in the MOD file shown in the final two images. While staying true to the spirit of the original, this updated version incorporates modern improvements, such as the use of non-radioactive paint and the inclusion of sapphire crystal, as detailed below. This watch combines the historical design and functional integrity of its predecessors with modern upgrades to meet the needs of today's professionals and enthusiasts.

watches.description: SKU Code: GMT/SS/B/QZ This stainless-steel GMT dual time zone watch is one of our latest models and is powered by the high-performance Ronda 515.24 quartz GMT movement . It features an anti-reflective, impact-resistant sapphire crystal , a scratch-resistant ceramic bezel , and a robust 300m / 1000ft water-resistant steel case . The watch is perfectly suitable for swimming, snorkelling, and general water sports. While the water resistance itself is more than adequate for diving, it’s worth noting that—as a GMT watch—the bezel is designed for tracking a second time zone rather than dive timing, so its functionality is more limited for that specific purpose. GMT Function Explained The appeal of a GMT watch lies not in complexity, but in its elegant simplicity. On a conventional watch, the hour hand completes one full rotation every 12 hours. A GMT watch adds a second hour hand that completes just one rotation every 24 hours . A corresponding 24-hour scale —usually on the bezel—allows the wearer to read a second time zone at a glance. Because the GMT hand operates on a true 24-hour cycle, there is no ambiguity between a.m. and p.m., making it exceptionally intuitive and easy to use. This is also why GMT watches can, at first glance, resemble diver’s watches. Designed for Aviation & Long-Range Travel These watches were originally developed for long-haul airline pilots and military transport aircrew , including those flying aircraft such as the C-130 Hercules and Airbus A400M . The GMT function allows pilots to instantly reference both departure and destination time zones—an essential requirement for long-range operations. We’re often asked why sapphire crystal is superior to standard mineral glass. Simply put, synthetic sapphire is the strongest and most scratch-resistant material available for watch crystals . From our experience, over 90% of cracked crystals we encounter—even with hardened mineral glass—are mineral rather than sapphire. Sapphire crystals are exceptionally durable because they are heat-treated to remove internal stresses , then finished with dual anti-reflective coatings for clarity and strength. These characteristics make sapphire especially popular with military personnel, security professionals, police officers , and those with active outdoor lifestyles—groups that account for over 70% of our customer base . It’s no coincidence that sapphire crystal is now also used on the latest iPhone models. Sapphire does come at a higher cost, which is why it’s typically reserved for higher-end watches —but in demanding environments, the durability more than justifies it.

watches.name: MWC Classic 1950s/1960s Pattern 25 Jewel Automatic "Adventurer" Watch with 200m Water Resistance and Retro Luminous Paint and Sapphire Crystal
watches.description: SKU Code: RE25J/54 This watch is based on a 1950s/1960s pattern exploration and adventurer watch. It features a box sapphire crystal that closely resembles the original plexiglass crystal. The movement is a Ronda R 150 or equivalent, a sophisticated 25-jewel automatic movement with an impressive frequency of 28,800 vibrations per hour (4Hz). This precision-crafted mechanism boasts a substantial 38-hour power reserve, ensuring enduring performance. Notably, it is equipped with hacking and hand-winding capabilities, exemplifying both efficiency and convenience. The watch uses Luminova instead of the Tritium that was used in the 1960s. The main advantage of Luminova is that, unlike Tritium, it does not deteriorate with age and is non-radioactive. This variant features paint that mimics the appearance of aged Tritium paint. The watch measures 39mm in diameter and comes fitted with a black NATO strap It also pairs exceptionally well with other NATO options, as shown in the images shared by a serving air force officer who wears this model as his daily watch. Dimensions and Specifications: Case Material: Stainless Steel Width (Excluding Crown): 36 mm Width (Including Crown): 39.5 mm Thickness (with Crystal): 13.3 mm Lug to Lug: 43.5 mm Water Resistance: 200m / 660ft Movement: 25 Jewel Ronda R 150 or equivalent Power Reserve: 38 hours Crown: Screw-down locking crown Caseback: Screw Crystal: Sapphire Crystal * Paint: Luminova Strap: Black NATO Strap Benefits of Sapphire Crystal: Many people ask about the advantages of sapphire crystal over the original plexiglass. Synthetic sapphire is by far the best material for watch crystals due to its strength, shatter-resistance, and scratch-resistance. These characteristics make it highly appealing to military and security personnel, police officers, and people who lead active outdoor lifestyles—groups that account for over 70% of our customers. The original plexiglass crystals, made of plastic/acrylic, used in the 1960s had the drawback of being easily scratched and susceptible to cracking upon impact. Additionally, they greatly limited the water resistance of the watch. Over 90% of cracked crystal incidents involve watches with mineral glass or plexiglass. Even hardened mineral crystals do not match sapphire's durability under adverse conditions. Sapphire crystals are strong because they are heat-treated to remove internal stresses, which can cause weakness. The crystals are then made into watch faces and coated with two layers of anti-reflective material. Interestingly, sapphire crystal is now used on the latest iPhones. While sapphire crystal comes at a higher price, it is typically found in higher-end watches due to its superior durability.

While based on the proven specifications used by other NATO chronograph manufacturers, this model brings several smart upgrades that improve functionality, legibility, and real-world practicality. This model uniquely blends new and traditional technology, retaining all the popular features of our conventional G10 Luminova models while incorporating cutting-edge self-luminous GTLS tritium vials. Key Features: Superior Night Visibility: The self-luminous system ensures exceptional readability at night. This model has a distinctive face layout, with the hour and minute hands each containing a brightly glowing vial of Tritium gas. The 12 o'clock position features an orange tube to assist with orientation if the watch is off the wrist, the other tubes are green. The vials contain less than the personal limit of 25 millicuries of radioactive gas, complying with U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission regulations (10 CFR 30.15). Tritium GTLS Tubes: These military-grade watches are the most readable in low light or total darkness, thanks to the self-activated light source, which is up to 100 times brighter than traditional luminous paint. These light-emitting tubes require no battery power, charging, or maintenance, and have a life expectancy of at least 10 years. Special Covert Matte Black PVD Finish: This finish is often specified in military contracts for special forces units, anti-terrorist units, and various covert operations. The PVD process alters the color of the steel at a molecular level, making it vastly superior to painted finishes that can fade or rub off.
